slides.0.title: Introducing Greek Wine
slides.0.subtitle: History, culture and modern revival
slides.1.title: Why study Greek wine?
slides.1.highlights.0.title: One of Europe's oldest wine cultures
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Wine in Greece has a history measured in millennia, and Dionysian worship and the symposium run deep in the classical world
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Over 300 native varieties
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Over 300 native varieties are documented and around 200 are still grown, making Greece one of the most varietally diverse countries
slides.1.highlights.2.title: 33 PDOs and 114 PGIs
slides.1.highlights.2.content: A full appellation system, and a regulatory framework to know precisely for the WSET Diploma (counts follow the current official lists)
slides.1.highlights.3.title: A region in renaissance
slides.1.highlights.3.content: An appellation system from the 1970s and a new generation of growers have raised quality and visibility
slides.1.content: Greece is the Old World's oldest yet most "emerging" wine country: ancient history, but international visibility built only in recent decades.
slides.2.title: From ancient Greece to the Middle Ages
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Dionysus and the symposium
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The ancient Greeks wove wine into religion, social life and medicine; the symposium was a central social ritual
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Mediterranean trade
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Greek wine travelled by sea across the Mediterranean, and colonisation spread viticulture
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The medieval Malvasia golden age
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Malvasia, named for Monemvasia, was famed across medieval Europe
slides.2.content: The name "Malvasia" survives in many regions today, tracing back to Greece's medieval trade.
slides.3.title: Decline and revival
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Decline under Ottoman rule
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Ottoman rule (roughly the 15th–19th centuries) and later conflict long held the industry back
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Retsina and the bulk-wine image
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Pine-resin Retsina is a traditional style, but a 20th-century cheap, bulk image dragged down international perception
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The appellation system of the 1970s
slides.3.highlights.2.content: An appellation system (OPAP etc.) from 1971 laid the foundation for a quality-led shift
slides.3.highlights.3.title: A new generation and native varieties
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Foreign-trained winemakers, boutique estates and the rediscovery of native grapes drove the modern revival
slides.3.content: This history explains why Greece today shows both an ancient tradition and a modern boutique face.
slides.4.title: Greek wine at a glance
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.4.highlights.0.content: About 64,000 ha of wine-grape vineyard (July 2022, Greek Ministry data) and roughly 2.1 million hl produced in 2022
slides.4.highlights.1.title: White-led
slides.4.highlights.1.content: White wine is about 70% of output
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Mountain vineyards
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Around 80% of the country's land is covered by high mountains; many vineyards sit in the hills
slides.4.content: Figures are recent approximations; check the latest official statistics before quoting.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Which best describes Greece's varietal diversity?
A. Only a few international varieties are grown
B. Over 300 native varieties documented, around 200 still grown
C. All of it is Assyrtiko
D. There are no native varieties
Greece is known for its many native varieties, a key difference from most wine countries.
Which wine, named for Monemvasia, was famed in medieval Europe?
"Malvasia" derives from Monemvasia, emblematic of the medieval Mediterranean sweet-wine trade.
Roughly when did Greece's modern appellation system begin?
OPAP and related rules began in 1971 and were later absorbed into the EU PDO/PGI framework.
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Producers' scale
slides.4.highlights.3.content: About 180,000 growers and more than 1,200 wineries (Wines of Greece)
